Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

We should not oil the hinge until the caretaker has looked at it, since he said the pin may need replacing. The sign by the wash station is still readable, but one corner has come loose and could snag a coat. I have put masking tape over that corner for now, and there is a fresh notice in the top drawer if anyone needs to replace the sign.

For the rack move, take the two loose baskets off first and put them on the bench, not on the floor where someone could trip over them. Well, if the floor is wet, use the rubber mat from beside the sink rather than a piece of cardboard.

1. Check that the north gate latch opens all the way before you bring the rack around.
2. Move the rack into B49 with the handles facing the shed door.
3. Return the baskets to the lower shelf and count them; there should be six.
4. Sweep up any grit from the drain cover and put the hand brush back on its peg.
5. Write down any damage you notice on the white board, but do not mark the brick wall with chalk because it takes a long time to wash off.

That should make the route usable without moving anyone else's bicycle.

Jasper mentioned that the delivery driver sometimes arrives early, and he said, “If the gate is shut, just leave the lock box on the shelf inside the side entrance.” We should keep the side entrance clear as well, since the folding chair has been left there twice this week. Jasper has the spare key in the small envelope marked shed, and he can open the gate if the latch sticks. Please do not leave that envelope on the workbench after he uses it; the bench gets cleared for the evening class, and loose keys can disappear into the tool trays.

The delivery is expected around eight on Thursday, so finish the rack move before seven thirty if possible. If the replacement locks arrive first, put the carton on the shelf above the sink and leave the packing slip on the clipboard. Do not open the carton or distribute the locks, because the caretaker needs to check the model numbers against the list in his office. The last shipment included two different sizes, and one of them was meant for the rear door. There are labels and a black marker in the desk drawer for marking the carton with the arrival date.

The pump pressure gauge is still working, though the needle sometimes settles slowly after someone uses it. Leave it attached and tell the next volunteer what you noticed rather than taking it apart. The patch kit is missing one small lever, so the repair group has ordered a replacement, but it has not arrived yet. If someone asks to borrow the kit, point out the empty slot and let them know that the tire levers in the jar by the window are available. The jar is not part of the kit and should stay on the sill, away from the damp floor.

After the move, check that the street door closes without hitting the rack and that the aisle between the bench and the bins remains wide enough for a bicycle to pass. Take a quick look at the notice board too, because the volunteer rota for next week is pinned underneath the shed rules. If the paper is curling, use one of the clear clips in the top drawer rather than adding another strip of tape. The caretaker will collect the old sign when he comes to inspect the hinge, so leave it in the folder marked notices.

Finally, the evening group is using the shed on Friday and needs the bench clear by six. Return the trolley to the office, hang the rubber mat beside the sink, and make sure the side entrance is closed when you leave. There is a small container of grit near the street door for the steps outside; it should remain there and not be brought into the shed. If the forecast rain continues, put the container under the short awning so it does not fill with water."}]
